nodes.text: Let $g(n)$ be the maximal size of $A\subseteq \{1,\ldots,n\}$ such that the products $\prod_{n\in S}n$ are distinct for all $S\subseteq A$. Is it true that\[g(n) \leq \pi(n)+\pi(n^{1/2})+o\left(\frac{x^{1/2}}{\log n}\right)?\]

#795 : [Er65] [Er69] [Er70b] [Er80,p.102] number theory Erdős proved [Er66] \[g(n) \leq \pi(n)+O\left(\frac{x^{1/2}}{\log n}\right).\]This upper bound would be essentially best possible, since one could take $A$ to be all primes and squares of primes. This was solved by Raghavan [Ra25] , who proved that\[g(n) \leq \pi(n)+\pi(n^{1/2})+O(n^{5/12+o(1)}),\]and also that\[g(n) \geq \pi(n)+\pi(n^{1/2})+\pi(n^{1/3})/3-O(1).\]In [Er80] Erdős made the stronger conjecture that\[g(n)=\pi(n)+\pi(n^{1/2})+\pi(n^{1/4})+\pi(n^{1/7})+\cdots,\]where $\pi(n^{1/k})$ occurs if and only if $F(k)>F(k-1)$, where $F(k)$ is the maximal size of a dissociated set in $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ (see [1] ). This is disproved by the lower bound of Raghavan. See also [786] .
